experiment_name: EVALUATION-ONLY ASU robustness check: PURE 96-game A_lr1e-4 champion vs 3xASUValueV1

algorithm_config.purpose: The champion (034's frozen 96-game A_lr1e-4 checkpoint) has so far only been measured against same-lineage PPO opponents (033/034). Does it hold up against ASU_FROZEN_TEACHER, a structurally different, non-learned opponent it never saw during training?
algorithm_config.asu_role: evaluation opponent only - no ASU action, value, or rollout output was recorded as a replay position, training label, or reward-shaping input; zero training/optimizer/backprop steps ran in this experiment
algorithm_config.design: One champion focus seat (deterministic legal-masked argmax, same policy every other champion-gate script in this project uses) + three copies of ASUValueV1 per game, rotated across all 4 physical seats. 4 fresh DEV seeds (53000-53003, evaluation_protocol.SEED_CLASS_DEV) x 4 seat rotations = 16 games, max_rounds=200. No promotion/GO-KILL decision rule was pre-registered - this is a descriptive robustness read, not a candidate-selection gate.
algorithm_config.asu_rollout_v1_family_skipped: ASURolloutV1 (a second, more expensive ASU family originally in scope) was informally calibrated before this run (DEV seed 42, not part of the registered seeds/games): ASUValueV1 completed a full 4-seat game in 170.8s (1043 decisions), but ASURolloutV1 only completed 13 decisions in a 120s budget (9.56s/decision average, worst 18.5s for a single decision). Extrapolated cost for the pre-registered 16-game ASURolloutV1 family was roughly 2-3 hours/game (~33-64+ hours total) - the user explicitly chose to skip it rather than run it at that cost. Zero ASURolloutV1 games were played.

metrics.not_a_promotion_claim: descriptive/diagnostic only, no GO/KILL rule was pre-registered - this is a robustness read on an unchanged champion, not a candidate comparison

result: The champion loses every single game: 0/16 wins (Wilson 95% CI [0.0, 19.4%]), 100% bankruptcy rate, and - unlike its round-200 net-worth-tiebreak-heavy record against same-lineage PPO opponents (033/034) - 0/16 round-cap hits, meaning every loss here is a genuine bankruptcy defeat, not a tiebreak. The champion's known BUY_PROPERTY/ACCEPT_TRADE collapse (0.0% and 0.0% respectively when legal, previously documented in 033/034 as diagnostic-only against same-lineage opponents) is lethal against ASUValueV1, which buys 69.1% of legal opportunities and accepts/declines trades with real discipline (17.96%/77.89%). The champion still spams trade offers (52.9/game) but never converts BUY_PROPERTY or ACCEPT_TRADE opportunities into board position, while ASUValueV1 builds full 28-property monopolies and extracts rent until the champion is bankrupt. The loss is uniform across all 4 physical seats (0/4 wins at every seat), ruling out a positional artifact. 0 illegal actions, 0 crashes, 0 fallbacks (no fallback/substitution mechanism exists for ASU in this harness - ASUValueV1's own selection logic only ever returns actions from its legal candidate set) across all 16 games. This directly contradicts the champion's strong record against same-lineage PPO opponents and shows it is NOT robust against a structurally different, competent, rule-following opponent - the win-rate advantage measured in 033/034 does not generalize outside this project's own self-play family.
notes: ASURolloutV1 (family A in the original 2-family pre-registration) was skipped entirely per the user's explicit choice after cost calibration - see algorithm_config.asu_rollout_v1_family_skipped; zero ASURolloutV1 games exist anywhere in this experiment. The champion checkpoint itself was not modified by this experiment - it remains the current champion; this result is evaluation evidence only, per CLAUDE.md's ASU-restrictions section (ASU sits as a fixed evaluation opponent only, never a training label, teacher, or fallback). No core algorithm file, evaluation_protocol.py's statistics, the champion checkpoint, or references/DeepRL_Monopoly (pinned at afd9205761317e196d77f679921c35fb04c7ab96) was modified to add this pre-registration or to record this result - only scripts/monopolyzero_a96_vs_asu_robustness_eval.py, its test file, evaluation_protocol.py's DEV_SEED_RANGES (53000-53003 registration), this log, and docs/EXPERIMENTS.md were added/changed (commits 7a1a5bf pre-registration, 288f737 an incidental test-isolation fix for a new ASU-import test file leaking ASU_FROZEN_TEACHER into sys.modules across the shared pytest process - unrelated to this experiment's own result). code_commit_sha (7a1a5bf1f60eec33c16ccdb7b0dbf4c7df53e04d) is the clean HEAD the runner itself captured via require_clean_git_tree() at process start, read directly from the script's own JSON output field git_head_sha, not backfilled. Wall time 7008.42s (~1h57m) is well above the ~35min estimate from a single-seed (DEV seed 42) calibration game - board-draw variance across the 4 fresh seeds (up to 2053 decisions in the longest game vs. 772 in the shortest) accounts for the difference; all 16 games nonetheless completed cleanly within the user-approved 2-hour hard budget.
